title: Legal test for what counts as a new build
shortTitle: What counts as a new build
headline: Proposed: a home is a new build if built on empty land, added to land, converted from non-residential use, or bought within 24 months of its first occupancy certificate.
summary: Negative gearing is still allowed on new builds, but the current law leaves the definition to a ministerial instrument that has not been made. The Tax Reform No. 3 Bill would write four tests into the law. It passed the House on 29 October 2026 and is before the Senate.

history.note: Budget tax explainer describes new builds

bigStat.caption: window to buy a newly built home and still count it as new

before: The current Act lets the Minister decide by legislative instrument what a new residential dwelling is. None had been made as at 20 November 2026.
after: If passed, a home is new if it is built on land with no dwelling, is an extra dwelling added to land, is converted from a non-residential building, or is bought within 24 months of its first certificate of occupancy where it was new for the seller.
The first certificate of occupancy must be issued at or after 7:30pm AEST 12 May 2026.
Specialist disability accommodation, community and public housing, active build-to-rent, and retirement villages and aged care would also be exempt from the negative gearing limit.

actions.text: Buying off the plan or a recently completed home? Keep the certificate of occupancy date and your contract and settlement dates.

sources.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 3) Bill 2026: bill homepage
Tax explainer: negative gearing and capital gains tax

caveats: The May Budget explainer described a 12-month window and excluded one-for-one knock-down rebuilds. The bill uses 24 months and treats some demolitions differently, so check the final law once passed.
